ch33.d.mode: Two polarizers, or three: one more between two crossed ones
ch33.d.theta: Angle $\theta$ of the turned polarizer from the axis of the first; dragging the white knob on its rim also changes it
ch33.p.goal.malus: A polarizer passes only the $\vec E$ component along its transmission axis. After the second one $I = I_1\cos^2\theta$ (Malus's law)
ch33.p.goal.three: A polarizer does not only filter, it also sets the new polarization direction, so a third sheet between crossed polarizers lets light through
ch33.p.obs.half: Unpolarized light ($\vec E$ in every direction) leaves the first polarizer vertically polarized, at half the intensity
ch33.p.obs.dial: Double arrows in the circles: the $\vec E$ oscillation seen head-on; length = amplitude ($\propto \sqrt{I}$)
ch33.p.obs.cross: Rotation 90°: crossed polarizers, no light gets through
ch33.p.obs.three: Three sheets at 45°: the middle one turns the polarization by 45° and $I = I_0/8$ gets through. At 0° or 90° the output is 0 again
ch33.p.assume.ideal: Ideal polarizers: the component along the axis passes fully, the perpendicular one is absorbed
ch33.d.n1: Upper medium the light comes from
ch33.d.n2: Lower medium the light refracts into
ch33.d.theta1: Angle $\theta_1$ between the incident ray and the normal; dragging the white dot at the ray's end also changes it
ch33.r.goal.snell: At the boundary part of the light reflects (angle of reflection = angle of incidence) and the rest refracts: $n_1\sin\theta_1 = n_2\sin\theta_2$
ch33.r.goal.tir: Going from a higher to a lower index, beyond the critical angle $\theta_c$ the refracted ray disappears: total internal reflection
ch33.r.obs.drag: Drag the white dot at the end of the ray to change the angle of incidence
ch33.r.obs.bend: Air → glass: bends toward the normal ($\theta_2 < \theta_1$). Glass → air: bends away from it
ch33.r.obs.crit: Glass → air (default): as the angle approaches 41.8° the refraction angle goes to 90°; beyond it, total reflection ($R = 100\%$)
ch33.r.obs.media: Diamond → air: critical angle only 24.4°, so light is easily trapped (why diamonds sparkle)
ch33.r.obs.width: Line width = intensity. Near the critical angle the reflected ray grows and the refracted ray fades
ch33.r.assume.fresnel: Intensities from the Fresnel reflectance for unpolarized light (mean of $s$ and $p$), no absorption
ch33.d.alpha: Angle $\alpha$ between the incoming ray and the fibre axis; dragging the white dot at the ray's end also changes it
ch33.f.goal.tir: An optical fibre guides light by repeated total internal reflection at the core wall, without loss
ch33.f.goal.accept: The wall angle $\theta$ exceeds the critical angle only if the entry angle $\alpha$ is below the acceptance angle $\alpha_\text{max}$
ch33.f.obs.guided: Default ($\alpha = 15°$): wall angle 80° > critical angle 76.7°, so the light is totally reflected all the way
ch33.f.obs.leak: Entry angle above the acceptance angle (about 20°): at every wall some light escapes into the cladding and the guided ray fades
ch33.f.obs.clad: Air cladding: a large index step makes the acceptance angle 90°, so any entry angle is guided
ch33.f.assume.flat: Straight fibre; refraction at the outer edge of the cladding is not drawn; the fibre diameter is enlarged
